target.title: fix(agents): follow through on promised asynchronous work
target.body:
Related: #58450

AI-assisted: yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent could promise to continue background or delegated work, end the turn without establishing a completion path, and leave the requester to ask again for the result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one shared prompt policy for the canonical full/minimal agent prompts and the standalone agent-bundle prompt. A promised follow-up now carries explicit ownership: arrange a push/watch completion path, keep the originating request open, proactively return with a result/link/proof or concrete blocker, and do not treat progress such as `running` as completion.

This is intentionally a prompt-policy fix, not a natural-language reply rewriter or runtime delivery gate. The broader runtime enforcement proposed in #58450 remains a separate product decision.

## User Impact

Agents using the default full, minimal, subagent, or agent-bundle prompts are explicitly instructed to close promised asynchronous work loops without waiting for another user nudge. Raw/custom replacement prompts retain their existing ownership semantics.

## Evidence

- The repaired PR diff is six agent prompt/test files with no dependency or generated-file changes.
- Focused Blacksmith Testbox proof passed 106 tests across `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/system-prompt.test.ts`, and `src/agents/sessions/system-prompt.test.ts`: [Actions run 29226477816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29226477816).
- A patch-identical full-checkout `pnpm check:changed` run passed core/core-test typechecks, changed-file lint and formatting, LOC ratchet, import-cycle checks, and repository guards: [Actions run 29226892402](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29226892402).
- Final branch sanity: current canonical `main` is an ancestor, the PR is mergeable, and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passes.
- Trusted mandatory autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- What was not tested: model compliance was not scored with a nondeterministic live provider.
